purpose: Native moving-platform overlap trace plus static carry-offset consumer decode.

static_callback.overlap_helper: 01F7:A075 is called by 01F7:9DC7 before the platform motion branch.
static_callback.accepted_shape: After the player-state helper returns nonnegative, A075 requires object_x < player_x < object_x + object_width and object_y <= player_y < object_y + 12. Accepted overlap writes DS:5006=-1.
static_callback.carry_helper: 01F7:A0B2 consumes nonzero DS:5006, computes DS:8816 as the platform horizontal fixed-point delta from object+0x2A, computes DS:8812 as platform_y - player_y + 1 fixed-point, then sets object+0x5A=FF and object+0x59=0.
player_consumers: 01F7:3FF8 adds DS:8812 to the player fixed-point Y and clears DS:8812.
01F7:3A8A/3B44 adds DS:8816 to the player fixed-point X and clears DS:8816.
static_callback.terminal_reset_decode: 01F7:9DC7 has no platform-specific authored terminal table: +0x52/+0x54 are wait counters, and 9F35/9F4A plus A03D/A051 select signed velocity reversals after MAP tests. The only callback removal is the camera rejection path A06F -> 1DEE.

controls: align object to live player with x=-8, y=-8 offsets

samples.interpretation: Accepted overlap initializes the native carry offsets; the platform itself does not move in this stationary state.
The carry latch enters its 0x14-tick phase while the callback remains active.

conclusions: The original platform callback performs a strict horizontal overlap plus a 12-pixel vertical band test; it is not an inert sprite-only path.
An accepted overlap publishes platform-to-player fixed-point carry offsets consumed by the native player update, and starts the platform carry latch.

The decoded callback has MAP-driven stop/reversal and wait phases, not a separate per-platform terminal table. Exact player-state preconditions for approaches outside the accepted band remain a narrower follow-up.
